components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single emphasized action in a task group.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { min-height: 30px; padding: 6px 12px; color: #fffdf8; background: #2f655f; border: 1px solid #2f655f; border-radius: 6px; font: 600 12px/1.4 'Yu Gothic UI', Meiryo, sans-serif; transition: background 120ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #254f4a; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #3e7e76; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.description: A frequent but non-primary workspace action.

narrative.overview: TSUZUNE should feel like returning to a familiar workbench: warm paper, dark green tools, and just enough structure to see where knowledge is connected. The interface is information-dense because the work is real, but its hierarchy must remain calm. Writing is the dominant surface; navigation and related context support it from the edges. The system rejects generic AI dashboards, decorative gradients, flashy glassmorphism, enterprise SaaS chrome, and unfamiliar controls invented for novelty. Motion is restrained to state feedback. At rest, the application is still.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper surfaces with one restrained deep-teal voice.
Compact controls and clear information hierarchy.
Flat tonal layering; elevation is reserved for temporary layers.
Familiar Windows behavior with strong keyboard focus.
Brand character comes from material, proportion, and a small thread mark—not decoration.

rules.name: The One Thread Rule
rules.body: Thread Teal is the only general accent and must remain visually scarce.

rules.name: The Writing Wins Rule
rules.body: Interface labels stay compact; the note is the content.

dos: Do preserve warm paper surfaces with WCAG AA text contrast.
Do keep Thread Teal scarce and meaningful.
Do use familiar line icons beside short Japanese labels.
donts: Don't turn TSUZUNE into a generic AI dashboard.
Don't use flashy glassmorphism, neon accents, or decorative motion.
Don't invent unfamiliar controls where Windows already has one.
Don't lock knowledge into an app-owned database.
